citation: Walther B, Chollet M. Menaquinones, Bacteria, and Foods: Vitamin K2 in the Diet. In: Vitamin K2 - Vital for Health and Wellbeing. IntechOpen; 2017, Table 1
note: The same lead author as walther-2013, revisiting the same primary studies four years later with a finer table: ranges where the earlier one gave a midpoint, and one row per primary study rather than one per food. Preferred over the earlier account wherever the two differ in granularity. Reference 6 in this table is Schurgers and Vermeer 2000; reference 32 is Kamao 2007.

legend.nd: not determined, per this table's own caption

conflict: The two accounts define their abbreviations differently. walther-2013 says plainly 'ND, not detectable' and marks natto MK-9 and MK-10, and sauerkraut MK-10, as ND. This table says 'nd, not determined' and marks natto MK-9 as nd and MK-10 as nr for every row drawn from reference 6. One account says the assay ran and found none; the other says it never ran. Where they disagree the weaker claim is the one this page makes, so those cells are recorded as not-measured rather than not-detected. Natto MK-9 is the exception: reference 6 reports a figure for MK-9 in sauerkraut, so the same assay plainly reached MK-9, and an empty natto cell from that study is an absence rather than a gap.
not-on-this-page: The table's other plant row is buckwheat, which sits under its Bread heading and is buckwheat bread rather than the cooked groats this page carries. Its MK-7 is 1.0 to 1.2 ug.
